title: Continuous Adaptive Batch Sculptor: kernel-aware admission & tail smoothing
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Reduce p95/p99 end-to-end latency for mixed-tenancy continuous workloads while preserving throughput and unit cost. Deliver a runtime component ("the Continuous Adaptive Batch Sculptor") that combines kernel hinting, light-weight attention path optimizations, and admission heuristics to: 1) route in-flight prefill/decodes to the lowest-latency kernel available, 2) shape admission to reduce harmful outliers without descheduling high-throughput tenants, and 3) smooth tail effects introduced by heterogeneous sequence-length bursts.

Design highlights:
- Kernel-aware admission: attach a small heuristic 'kernel-hint' to requests based on request features (model family, requested max tokens, presence of long context tokens, decode mode). The admission controller uses this to prefer grouping requests that are mutually kernel-friendly to avoid kernel-switch overhead during decode.
- Dynamic kernel probing: lightweight runtime sampler that profiles a small percentage of requests to validate kernel cost models (latency/throughput per batch shape). Probe results update the admission scoring in near-real-time (60s windows).
- Attention fast-path hints: detect common attention patterns (short prefix + long decode) and enable specialized fused-kernel paths for them; fall back to general kernels when patterns mismatch.
- Graceful tail smoothing: apply micro-throttles (0-5ms per-request delay) to specific admission buckets when p99 climbs, preserving average throughput but reducing variance. Throttles are tenant-aware and budgeted (no starvation).
- Prefill/Decode decoupling for long-context clients: allow prefill-heavy requests to be admitted on a separate prefill lane with larger batching window but protected decode slots to keep decode latency predictable.

Why different from existing batchers: Instead of a single admission objective (throughput or latency), the Sculptor uses multi-objective scoring combining kernel-fit, observed decode tail risk, and per-tenant fairness. We avoid global blocking by using soft isolation (per-tenant budgeted windows) and continuous re-evaluation via probing data.

Success metrics (tracked by feature flag):
- Reduce p95 E2E decode latency by >= 18% on mixed workloads (short chat + long-document generation)
- Reduce p99 E2E decode latency by >= 25% without >3% regression in overall throughput
- No >5% increase in token cost for affected tenants

Rollout plan:
1) Internal canary (runtime-1.20-alpha): 2 GPU hosts, non-customer workloads for 48 hours, validate latency/throughput and stability.
2) Beta customers by opt-in (two medium traffic tenants) for 7 days. Monitor SLOs, customer signals.
3) Gradual ramp with automated rollback if p99 > baseline + 20% for >30m.

Artifacts and links: design doc, benchmark dashboard, and initial PRs listed below.

Open questions / trade-offs considered:
- Per-tenant fairness vs. global throughput: we chose budgeted soft isolation to reduce tail risk without sacrificing packing efficiency.
- Kernel hint accuracy vs. request overhead: hints are computed from existing request metadata (no extra round-trip) and sampled probes keep the model calibrated.
- Micro-throttling magnitude: we limit to a few milliseconds to avoid changing client-side timeouts; if clients observe higher latencies we fallback to model-variant routing.

Implementation notes:
- New runtime components: admission-sculptor (admission scoring), kernel-prober (background sampler), lane-manager (manages prefill/ decode lanes).
- Data pipeline: prober & admission counters emitted to "metrics.streaming.kernel_fit" and "metrics.streaming.tail_risk", surfaced in Console dashboards.
- Config knobs (feature-flag driven): sculptor.enabled, sculptor.probe_rate, sculptor.max_micro_throttle_ms, sculptor.per_tenant_budget.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for admission scoring logic and budget accounting.
- Load test harness with synthetic mix (50% short chat, 20% long-prefill+decode, 30% medium generation) to validate p50/p95/p99 and throughput under bursts.
- Chaos test: simulate kernel failure (force fallback path) and ensure requests are rerouted within 5s and OOMs are handled gracefully.

Monitoring & Observability:
- Dashboards: Kernel-fit heatmaps, admission queue depth per lane, per-tenant tail-risk, end-to-end p50/p95/p99 by model.
- Alerts: p99 > baseline*1.3 for 10m (P0), probe success rate < 70% (P1).

Stakeholders: Jin (owner), Marco Ruiz (SRE reviewer), Priya Nair (PM), Emily Chen (Console UX).
